question: In the same kind of randomized experiment (plants randomly assigned to plant food or none), the data were re-randomized 100 times to simulate no treatment effect. A difference of 3 cm or more happened 40 times. What does this suggest about the plant food?
correct_answer: The difference could easily be due to chance, so the experiment does not give evidence that the plant food made a difference.

question: Why are the data re-randomized many times in the simulation?
choices: A. To remove outliers | B. To see what differences happen by chance alone | C. To make the mean larger | D. To make the treatment work better
correct_answer: To see what differences happen by chance alone

question: Random assignment helps make two treatment groups alike before an experiment begins.
A difference between two groups in one experiment is always caused by the treatment.
